Does this paper address the risk that the survey questionnaire, item content, or target population data used to prompt/evaluate the LLM were present in the model's training corpus (i.e., data leakage/training data contamination)? Classify the paper's approach using exactly one of the following categories, and quote the specific sentence(s) that justify your classification. If no relevant text exists, answer "Not addressed" and write "no supporting quote found."

Categories:
A — Not addressed: No discussion of leakage/contamination risk anywhere in the paper.
B — Acknowledged only: Authors mention leakage as a possible confound or limitation but describe no specific step taken to reduce it.
C — Temporal exclusion: Authors state or imply the survey/data/instrument postdates the model's training cutoff.
D — Novel/unpublished/proprietary instrument: Authors state the questionnaire or item set was newly created, unpublished, or not publicly indexed online, specifically to reduce leakage risk.
E — Concurrent primary data collection: Authors collected new human survey data at the same time as querying the LLM, using it as a leakage-resistant benchmark.
F — Memorization probe: Authors directly tested whether the model could reproduce/recognize the survey instrument or specific items (e.g., asked the model to recite items, canary-string test, verbatim-recall check).
G — Other mitigation: A leakage-reduction strategy not covered above (describe briefly).

Output format: `Category | Quote | Page/section if available.`
